label: label_inferable true
label_semantics: E-A: label_inferable of the NLI benchmark (retrieved_context_entailment: an expert judged the article opinion inferable from the four retrieved chunks), not a global truth label. E-B: the trecho_sustenta judgment of the udv_v1 annotation sample, the majority of three blind passes of a language model; it is not a human judgment, and agreement with it is not accuracy

premise.max: each distinct non-empty retrieved chunk is scored on its own with the opinion as hypothesis; the opinion score is the max over its chunks (an opinion with no non-empty chunk gets the minimum of the scorer: 0.0 for probabilities, the lowest score of the split for raw scores)
premise.concatenated: the non-empty chunks in order joined by one space, scored as one premise, only for candidates with concatenated = true; truncation from the end of the premise to max_length is counted and reported. Secondary: not in the Holm family
premise.domain_shift: E-A premises are four transcript chunks of about 630 characters each; E-B premises are one sentence. A result on one does not transfer to the other without this caveat

family: E-A validation, max pool: every candidate except cosine_serafim against cosine_serafim on roc_auc and on aurc, one Holm family over all these comparisons

laya.support_rule: the battery signals of these seven questions, each already oriented so that higher means more support (p1, p2: P(entailment), the reversed option order mapped back by name; p3, p4: P(true); p5, p6: P(same_position), mapped back by name; p7: expected coverage level / 4). p8_similarity is left out because the battery declares it a similarity question, not a support question
laya.aggregate_rule: per premise item, the mean, the median and the minimum of the support signals of the question set; the opinion score is the max over its non-empty items (E-A) or the value on the single evidence sentence (E-B). min is the conservative rule: it is high only when every question gives support
laya.spread_rule: per premise item, the population standard deviation of the support signals of the question set (and, reported with it, max minus min); the opinion spread is the one of the item with the highest mean aggregate (ties: first item). As a confidence signal it is read as -spread (higher = the questions agree more). As a flag, flagged = spread above the median spread of the E-A train opinions of the same scorer and question set; the share of negatives among flagged and unflagged items is reported with the hearing-bootstrap interval of their difference, in E-A (train and validation) and E-B with the same train threshold

refit_check.compared_with: final_test.json learned and results entries of the primary

train.bootstrap: 5000 hearing resamples, seed 42, percentile interval; replicates with a single class are skipped
train.note: descriptive: the Holm families are the validation ones; the E3x primary, and the rank combinations that use it, are in-sample on train

validation.bootstrap: 5000 hearing resamples, seed 42, percentile interval; replicates with a single class are skipped
